queue.goal: Turn Relay's production primitives into a durable resumable operation framework so agents invoke policy-defined workflows instead of manually conducting every GitHub, Cloudflare, Runner and QA step.
queue.acceptance: Every substantial workflow can create a stable operation_id with persisted stage/state, exact source/head/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, timestamps, retry/reconciliation history, blocker/waiting-for-human state and recovery/rollback state; reconnecting agents can resume from the durable receipt without reconstructing chat history; server-side recipes cover at least ship-change, publish-worker, qa-then-merge and rollback-release; ambiguous mutations reconcile by readback before retry; event/webhook updates can advance operation state without chat polling; release policy supports bounded canary/verify/promote/rollback semantics without protection bypass; operation status/history is queryable for UI; tool-surface growth stays minimal by preferring recipes/resources/contracts over one tool per step. Tool-pattern contract: operation recipes and their exposed tool interfaces consume the Relay 1.9.8 tool-design standard derived from Arcade's Agentic Tool Patterns. Recipes should prefer explicit task bundles/tool chains over forcing agents to manually orchestrate repetitive low-level calls, expose durable operation IDs and progressive status, classify failures with retry/user/auth/permanent semantics plus recovery guidance, preserve idempotent/readback/transaction boundaries, keep outputs structured/token-efficient, and enforce permission/secret/scope rules server-side. Deviations from applicable patterns must be explicit and justified; do not multiply tools merely to satisfy a pattern mechanically.
queue.next_action: Define the operation/receipt schema and transition invariants first, but consume the Relay 1.9.8 agentic-tool standard for recipe/tool boundaries, errors, discovery, output shaping and security. Reuse existing source/cloud/verify primitives and prefer durable high-level recipes where they eliminate fragile manual tool chains.

queue.goal: Ship Relay 1.8 as the contextual MCP experience and liveness release: ordinary Relay work should surface compact interactive cards for the relevant Runner, Inspector, Source and Cloud context, while every long-running operation exposes durable progress, heartbeat and stuck-state visibility so the user never has to guess whether a worker is still moving.
queue.acceptance: Canonical service/version metadata and release-facing UI/docs identify the resulting release as Relay 1.8.0. ChatGPT can render compact contextual cards for at least Runner project/assignment/preflight state, Source pull request/check/merge state, Cloud release/deployment state, Inspector evidence/review/human-QA state, and durable multi-step operations; cards preserve exact artifact/operation identity, refresh in place where the client supports it, and expand into the shared Relay app/fullscreen view instead of creating parallel mini-products. Cards clearly distinguish queued, working, waiting-on-external-system, waiting-for-human, blocked, stale/unresponsive, failed, rolled-back and complete states. Long-running active operations persist a meaningful heartbeat/updated_at plus human-readable current stage and next action at least every 10 minutes while work is genuinely progressing. By default, 20 minutes without a meaningful heartbeat/progress signal marks an active operation stale; the threshold may be configurable by operation class but must never silently extend itself. Crossing into blocked, failed, stale, waiting-for-human or complete emits one durable notification/attention event; repeated checks do not spam unless the state materially changes. If GitHub/Cloudflare/another dependency is still demonstrably running, Relay says so instead of falsely labeling the worker frozen; if the worker actually stopped heartbeating or hit quota/rate/auth/tool failure, Relay says that plainly and includes the last successful stage plus recovery action. Operation receipts persist stage/state, exact source/head/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, timestamps, retry/reconciliation history and waiting/blocker reasons so reconnecting clients can resume without chat history. Human-QA cards consume the existing Runner QA-helper/Visuals contracts and remain bound to exact evidence identity. Existing headless tools remain compatible; contextual UI is additive. Runner and Inspector retain the 1.7 identities/icons. Web and MCP surfaces use the same state model. Mobile/desktop layouts remain usable. Required tests, exact-head admission, MCP/web rendering checks and authenticated production readback pass before completion.

First stabilize the durable operation/receipt and progress-event model, including heartbeat/stale semantics and attention events; then bind contextual output templates/cards to existing Relay tools and the shared app, preserve 1.7 Runner/Inspector identity, validate exact-head behavior, ship as Relay 1.8.0, and leave a durable completion receipt.

queue.goal: Ship Relay 1.7.5 as an independently deployable observed-progress backend release that gives Relay one canonical, evidence-backed answer to 'what is actually happening right now?' before the 1.8 UI lands. Build the server-side progress/operation piping that 1.8 consumes; do not depend on or implement the 1.8 dashboard/card presentation.
queue.acceptance: Release-facing metadata identifies the backend release as Relay 1.7.5 and it can merge/deploy independently while relay-1.8-contextual-ui-20260930 continues on its separate UI-only scope. Introduce a canonical observed-progress model/receipt/event stream that reconciles Runner coordination state with concrete GitHub and Cloudflare evidence instead of treating claim state, next_action prose, lease presence, or declaration time as execution progress. Each tracked operation/assignment exposes a canonical stage, latest concrete progress event, last meaningful progress timestamp, worker heartbeat/freshness separately from external-system activity, exact known source/base/head/branch/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, waiting/blocker reason, and recovery action. The model must distinguish at least reserved-but-idle, working, waiting-on-external-system, waiting-for-human, blocked, possibly-stale, officially-stale/unresponsive, failed, rolled-back, and complete. A live GitHub/Cloudflare job must prevent false 'worker frozen' conclusions while still showing that the worker itself is waiting; a dead heartbeat, quota/rate/auth/tool failure must be represented plainly with last successful stage and recovery. Implement the 5-minute meaningful-heartbeat target, 10-minute possibly-stale evaluation, and 20-minute official-stale default as backend semantics/configurable policy, without silently extending stale thresholds. Persist durable progress events/receipts so reconnecting clients can reconstruct the timeline without chat history; repeated observations of unchanged state must not spam duplicate events. Add reconciliation logic for obvious coordination drift: completed/absorbed/superseded intent must be classifiable separately from live work, orphan/unregistered branches must be surfaced as reconciliation findings, and umbrella/held reservations must not be presented as active execution merely because they still occupy policy capacity. Expose a stable backwards-compatible MCP/API contract that 1.8 can consume for project/assignment/operation progress and recent events; existing 1.7 tools/clients continue to work. This release does not redesign dashboard/cards and must not write 1.8 UI files. Tests must cover Runner-only reserved state versus observed work, GitHub check/PR waits, Cloudflare deploy waits, heartbeat freshness, stale transitions, deduped events, exact identity propagation, drift/reconciliation classification, and 1.8 consumer contract shape. Required install/tests, exact-head admission, merge, exact-source deployment, runtime readback and durable completion receipt must pass.
queue.next_action: Claim this as soon as a branch slot is legitimately available, without taking over or folding into the active 1.8 branch. Implement the canonical progress schema/event receipt first, then evidence adapters/reconciliation for Runner + GitHub + Cloudflare, then expose the stable consumer API/tool contract. Keep all UI rendering in 1.8. Before completion, leave a precise consumer handoff in docs/relay/RELAY_1_7_5_RELEASE.md describing the fields/events 1.8 must bind to and explicitly stating that UI must not infer progress from claim state or next_action prose.

queue.acceptance:
Relay 1.9 ships as a patch train with these canonical capabilities:

- relay.SKILLS: deterministic JIT resolution, bounded context, provenance/license/integrity metadata, capability gating, project-private overlays, safe upstream audit/update, and composable creative/platform/performance/GitHub/Cloudflare skills. Creative coverage includes aesthetic direction, IA/flow, motion, visual QA, optimization, web, macOS, Windows, Android and GNOME; Figma-bound skills use the real dependency when available.
- worker communication: inspect sibling live state first; classify FYI/request/blocker/decision/handoff/scope-change; cite exact project/assignment/branch/PR/evidence identity; communicate context, impact and requested action; reconcile received messages against canonical state before acting; avoid duplicate/no-op chatter. Messages never silently change ownership/scope: Runner amend/rescope/handoff remains authoritative.
- organization-first narration: later coordination successors must consume canonical staff identity and describe people + ownership + outcome + validation by default; preserve machine IDs/evidence underneath and keep low-level transport/tool/SHA detail subordinate unless directly relevant. Separately, the Inspector QA surface must implement the user-approved Figma node 59:115 review instrument as the visible card: ~450px default width, compact single-column composition, project pill, progress, one question/reason, binary answer surfaces, note field, and no persistent chrome (no inspector masthead, move/minimize/close buttons, preview/capture status rows, flow badge, previous/next row, separate Overall UI, technical details, save footer, or visible resize handle). The card must autosave, be draggable from non-interactive card regions, resize responsively through invisible edge/corner hit zones, remain clamped on viewport resize, and dock to any viewport edge leaving only a thin real card edge visible. A docked edge gives a restrained occasional idle wiggle plus one return wiggle after meaningful pointer inactivity; prefers-reduced-motion removes the wiggle. The docked edge adapts contrast to the content beneath it: soft off-white glow over dark content, near-black shadow over light content, and a conservative dual-contrast fallback when tone cannot be known. Captured image/video surfaces may sample luminance when safe; live cross-origin previews use an optional postMessage tone handshake and must degrade safely if unavailable. Inspector's review surface behaves like Field's canvas without importing Field's editor runtime: regular wheel/two-finger pan, Ctrl/Cmd+wheel or trackpad pinch zoom at the pointer, middle-mouse pan, Space+drag pan, initial fit-to-view, GPU transforms, and responsive reclamping. Live embeddable previews are the primary QA surface; video then image are fallbacks/evidence. The live page must receive pointer, keyboard, forms, scrolling and navigation normally, with Inspector camera gestures not stealing ordinary page interaction. Full-screen exit is owned by the viewport, not the review card: Escape, browser Back/history state, and a small viewport-only reveal affordance near the safe corner provide exit paths. Existing evidence identity, autosave persistence, deterministic QA gates and live-preview resolver/session contracts remain canonical; do not create a second evidence store. Inline ChatGPT cards must also be able to show existing Inspector QA evidence that Relay already captured: when a verification result or selected evidence record has an authorized screenshot URL/evidence ID, the compact card may render that screenshot directly inside the card with a clear QA/evidence caption and exact evidence identity. The card must not invent or substitute images; it must degrade cleanly to the text/status card when no image is available or the host cannot load it. The MCP App resource CSP must explicitly allow only the Relay-controlled image origins required for these QA screenshots, following the current Apps SDK resource-domain contract.

claims.acceptance:
Relay 1.9 ships as a patch train with these canonical capabilities:

- relay.SKILLS: deterministic JIT resolution, bounded context, provenance/license/integrity metadata, capability gating, project-private overlays, safe upstream audit/update, and composable creative/platform/performance/GitHub/Cloudflare skills. Creative coverage includes aesthetic direction, IA/flow, motion, visual QA, optimization, web, macOS, Windows, Android and GNOME; Figma-bound skills use the real dependency when available.
- worker communication: inspect sibling live state first; classify FYI/request/blocker/decision/handoff/scope-change; cite exact project/assignment/branch/PR/evidence identity; communicate context, impact and requested action; reconcile received messages against canonical state before acting; avoid duplicate/no-op chatter. Messages never silently change ownership/scope: Runner amend/rescope/handoff remains authoritative.
- organization-first narration: later coordination successors must consume canonical staff identity and describe people + ownership + outcome + validation by default; preserve machine IDs/evidence underneath and keep low-level transport/tool/SHA detail subordinate unless directly relevant. Relationship adaptation stays Julian/lead-managed; no canned joke bank.
- assignment taxonomy: durable amendable category, labels, tags and designated role metadata. Controlled categories include architecture, design, implementation, research, QA/verification, maintenance, release and coordination. Labels are structured cross-cutting metadata; tags are bounded freeform discovery/context metadata. One primary role plus optional supporting roles may drive skill selection/communication posture but never authorization. Role metadata is separate from sticky staff identity; names come from the canonical staff directory. Expose taxonomy/roles to routing, filtering, UI and resume checkpoints.
- live amendment sync: active workers/chats consume only new relevant canonical amendments from a monotonic cursor at bounded synchronization points; unchanged checks inject nothing, and scope-changing/blocking updates reconcile before conflicting work continues.
- safe assignment amendments: stable identity/ownership, immutable claimed branch/base, CAS/readback, conflict-safe scope changes, bounded who/when/what/why history. Planning skills amend canonical state rather than hand-edit it.
- findings-ledger routing: classify adopt/defer/reject/supersede; route adopted findings into the safest existing assignment or deliberate successor; maintain RFS linkage/status. Ledger is planning input, not automatic backlog.
- low-overhead resume checkpoints from canonical evidence: assignment/branch/base/head, changed paths, commits, PR/check/deploy stage, last successful action, blockers/waits, next action, QA context, ledger refs and exact evidence identities; dedupe unchanged state and expose latest-valid resume.
- universal meaningful x.x.# cadence: test/admit exact source; merge; deploy if applicable; verify runtime/readback; refresh integrations/consumer when needed; verify the new surface; continue from canonical state.
- valid work must not be blocked by file/document/context/request-size ceilings: switch automatically to patch/edit, append, bounded chunks, indexed/sharded logical docs and deterministic reassembly while preserving ownership/provenance/CAS safety.
- preserve Relay 1.8 UI contracts: human headline + short description, subordinate technical detail, specific QA asks, live previews when viable with exact identity.

Tests cover taxonomy/roles, communication/handoffs, amendments, ledger routing, resume, size-safe transport, skill gating and UI/QA. No parallel state store, giant permanent prompt dump, one-tool-per-skill explosion or new standing credentials.
